subject: history_social
passage: For centuries in Europe, barbers did more than cut hair: they also pulled teeth and performed bloodletting, a treatment that doctors of the time believed could cure many ailments. The striped pole outside a barbershop is traditionally said to recall that history. Each part of the design has a meaning: the red stripe stands for ______ the white stripe, for the bandages that were wrapped around a patient's arm; and the pole itself, for the staff a patient gripped to make the veins stand out. Whether or not every detail of the story is true, the sign outlasted the surgery by hundreds of years.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The sentence lists three parts of the design, and the second and third items already contain commas ("the white stripe, for the bandages …"). When items in a list contain commas, the items are separated by semicolons, as the semicolon after "arm" shows. The first item, "the red stripe stands for blood," must therefore end with a semicolon too.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "And" belongs only before the last item of a list, and the items here are separated by semicolons, not commas.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The items in this list already contain commas, so another comma would leave the reader unable to tell where one item ends and the next begins.
explanation.C: Correct. The semicolon separates the first item from the second, matching the semicolon already used before "and the pole itself."
explanation.D: Incorrect. A colon introduces a list; it can't separate one item of a list from the next.
